tools.name: check_ai_recommendation
tools.description: Use this when a business owner asks whether ChatGPT or AI recommends their business, whether AI tools like ChatGPT or Perplexity mention or suggest their business, why AI recommends their competitors instead, or how to get their business recommended by AI. It runs a small real check: it asks ChatGPT

tools.name: get_ai_recommendation_result
tools.description: Use this to get the result of a check started with check_ai_recommendation, using the check_id it returned. Returns the status (queued, running, done, failed or refused). When done: for ChatGPT and Perplexity, how many of their answers named the business, which businesses they named instead, and one

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "check_ai_recommendation" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Use this when a business owner asks whether ChatGPT or AI recommends their business, whether AI tools like ChatGPT or Perplexity mention or suggest their busine…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_ai_recommendation · Public sink: check_ai_recommendation.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_ai_recommendation · Public sink: check_ai_recommendation

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
